newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian premier Kostov leaves for Brussels.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian premier Kostov leaves for Brussels.

text.p: Bulgaria's reformist Prime Minister Ivan Kostov left on Tuesday for a three-day official visit to Brussels to seek support for reforms and to promote investment opportunities in his crisis-ridden country.

"Our main goal is to acquaint the European Union with the course of reforms in Bulgaria and get support for those reforms," Foreign Minister Nadezhda Mihailova, who is accompanying Kostov, told reporters.
This is Kostov's first visit abroad since taking office on May 21 after his Union of Democratic Forces swept to victory in April 19 general elections.

He is due to meet European Commission President Jacques Santer, External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek and European Parliament president Jose Maria Gil-Robles, hoping to press his country's bid for early admission in the EU and NATO.
Bulgaria has an associate membership agreement with the EU.
